newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors summon former defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors summon former defence minister.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Thursday summoned former defence minister Lee Yang-ho, who was sacked last week, to question him over an arms scandal, witnesses said.
"Lee arrived at the prosecutors' office for questioning this evening," a Reuters photographer said.
"Lee did not respond to reporters' questions and was taken to a prosecutor office," the photographer said.
President Kim Young-sam dismissed Lee last week, hours before the main opposition party National Congress for New Politics accused him of taking bribes. Kim has ordered an inquiry.

The National Congress charged that Lee and a Korean-American arms dealer split a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Daewoo admitted giving money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe. Lee has denied accusations of wrongdoing.
